description: Find the minimum-cost closed tour that visits each city exactly once and returns to the starting point.
example: A technician must visit every client site once and return to the depot.

description: Determine minimum-cost vehicle routes that start and end at a depot while respecting vehicle capacity limits.
example: Delivery trucks must serve customers without exceeding load limits.

description: Plan vehicle routes so each customer is served within a specified time window while routing constraints are satisfied.
example: Grocery delivery requires visiting households within scheduled 2-hour windows.

description: Plan routes that satisfy paired pickup and drop-off requests, including pairing, pickup-before-delivery precedence, and possible timing, capacity, or service-quality constraints.
example: A courier or paratransit operator must pick up passengers or parcels and deliver them to paired destinations.

description: Select a subset of nodes to visit and construct feasible routes to maximize collected reward under route length or time limits.
example: A tourist route planner selects the best attractions under time limits.

description: Simultaneously optimize vehicle routing and inventory replenishment decisions over time.
example: A vendor must decide when and where to deliver fuel to gas stations.

description: Find the minimum-cost path between a source node and a destination node in a network.
example: Navigation software computes the fastest route to your destination.

description: Connect all nodes with minimum total edge cost while avoiding cycles.
example: Building a low-cost fiber-optic communication network.

description: Connect selected terminal nodes with minimum total cost, allowing additional intermediate nodes when beneficial.
example: Designing power distribution lines with added junction points.

description: Find the maximum amount of flow that can be sent from a source to a sink through a capacitated network.
example: Determine the maximum water that can flow through a pipe system.

description: Send required flow through a capacitated network at minimum total transportation or operating cost.
example: Optimizing product shipments in a logistics network.

description: Assign agents to tasks with minimum total cost or maximum total benefit, usually with one-to-one assignment constraints.
example: Assigning workers to machines to minimize processing time.

description: Assign tasks, items, vehicles, or workloads to agents, bins, or resources while respecting capacity or availability limits and assignment-dependent costs or benefits.
example: Assign workloads or aircraft types to limited resources while satisfying capacity and operational constraints.

description: Assign facilities to locations to minimize interaction flow multiplied by pairwise distance costs.
example: Placing departments in a factory to minimize transportation effort.

description: Select items to maximize total value without exceeding a capacity limit.
example: Selecting advertisements given limited budget.

description: Assign selected items to multiple capacity-limited knapsacks or bins to maximize total value.
example: Assigning shipments to trucks of different capacities.

description: Select items to maximize total value while satisfying multiple resource or capacity constraints.
example: Selecting projects with limits on budget, labor, and equipment.

description: Pack all items into the fewest number of bins without exceeding bin capacities.
example: Loading packages into the smallest number of delivery trucks.

description: Cut raw materials into required sizes or patterns while minimizing waste or material usage.
example: Cutting steel rolls into custom widths with minimum scrap.

description: Pack rectangles into a strip of fixed width while minimizing the used height or length.
example: Arranging ads on a newspaper page to minimize page length.

description: Select the fewest or minimum-cost sets so that each required element is covered at least once or to a required coverage level.
example: Choose minimal warehouse locations, teams, or bundles to cover all required zones, skills, or preferences.

description: Select mutually disjoint sets to maximize total value or the number of selected sets.
example: Choosing non-overlapping marketing campaigns.

description: Select disjoint sets so that every element is covered exactly once.
example: Assigning flight crews so every flight is covered without overlap.

description: Schedule jobs consisting of ordered operations on specific machines to optimize completion time or related performance measures.
example: Scheduling complex manufacturing processes across machines.

description: Schedule jobs that all follow the same machine order, usually to minimize makespan or total completion time.
example: Assembly line scheduling in automotive production.

description: Schedule operations that can be processed in any order while ensuring each job and machine handles at most one operation at a time.
example: Laboratory experiments that require shared equipment.

description: Assign and sequence jobs on multiple machines, which may be identical, uniform, or unrelated.
example: Distributing computational tasks across cloud servers.

description: Schedule job operations when each operation may be processed by one of several alternative machines.
example: Manufacturing where machines can substitute for each other.

description: Schedule project tasks with precedence constraints to determine or minimize project duration.
example: Construction project planning with task dependencies.

description: Schedule project tasks with precedence constraints under limited renewable or nonrenewable resources.
example: Assigning workers and equipment in a construction project.

description: Select facility sites and assign demand to facilities to minimize opening, service, or transportation costs.
example: Choosing distribution center locations.

description: Place k facilities to minimize total or average customer distance to the nearest selected facility.
example: Choosing k hospitals to reduce average travel time.

description: Place k facilities to minimize the maximum distance from any customer to its nearest selected facility.
example: Selecting disaster relief hubs to minimize worst-case response time.

description: Select hub nodes and allocate flows through hubs to minimize total transportation or connection cost.
example: Airline hub-and-spoke network design.

description: Select network edges, arcs, lines, capacities, or service levels to minimize cost while satisfying connectivity, flow, demand, or service requirements.
example: Design a telecommunications backbone or transit network by selecting links or lines under budget and service constraints.

description: Assign colors to nodes so adjacent nodes receive different colors, often minimizing the number of colors used.
example: Assigning wireless frequencies to avoid interference.

description: Find the largest or highest-weight subset of nodes that are all pairwise connected.
example: Detecting tightly clustered communities in a social network.

description: Find the largest or highest-weight subset of nodes with no edges between any selected pair.
example: Selecting non-conflicting events in a schedule.

description: Select a limited number of sets to maximize the number or weight of covered elements.
example: Choosing store locations to maximize population coverage.

description: Allocate investments to optimize expected return, risk, or diversification under budget and risk constraints.
example: Choosing a stock portfolio with volatility constraints.

description: Choose an order quantity under uncertain demand to balance shortage and overstock costs.
example: Retailer ordering newspapers with uncertain demand.

description: Determine production or order quantities over multiple periods to meet demand while minimizing setup, production, and inventory costs.
example: Factory planning weekly production to meet fluctuating demand.

description: Optimize decisions when uncertain parameters are represented by probability distributions or scenarios.
example: Deciding power generation with uncertain renewable output.

description: Optimize decisions to remain feasible or perform well under worst-case realizations within an uncertainty set.
example: Allocating resources when demand is uncertain but bounded.

description: Optimize upper-level decisions while accounting for lower-level decisions that are themselves solutions to another optimization problem.
example: Setting toll prices while users choose shortest paths.

description: Optimize multiple potentially conflicting objectives and characterize trade-offs among them.
example: Balancing delivery cost and service quality in routing.

description: Optimize staffing, capacity, routing, admission, or service decisions in systems with waiting lines or queueing networks.
example: Staffing cashiers to minimize customer waiting time.

description: Schedule tasks or services so that each activity occurs within its allowed time interval while satisfying resource or sequencing constraints.
example: Assigning maintenance time slots to minimize machine downtime.

description: Determine production quantities of one or more products to maximize profit or minimize cost under resource, demand, and capacity constraints.
example: A factory produces two furniture types using limited labor and wood; decide production levels to maximize profit.

description: Allocate limited resources such as time, labor, budget, production, seats, electricity, or capacity among activities, contracts, or demands to maximize benefit or minimize cost.
example: Allocate limited production, labor, or capacity across competing demands while satisfying resource and requirement constraints.

description: Mix raw materials or choose component proportions to minimize cost or optimize quality while meeting component, property, or specification constraints.
example: Blend two types of crude oil to satisfy sulfur and octane requirements at minimum cost.

description: Select quantities of foods or ingredients to satisfy nutritional requirements at minimum cost.
example: Choose daily food portions to meet protein and vitamin constraints while minimizing total spending.

description: Optimize dimensions or shapes of geometric objects to minimize cost, material use, surface area, or packaging waste under volume or performance requirements.
example: Find the height and radius of a cylindrical can that minimizes material cost while holding 1 liter.

description: Determine generator on/off schedules, startup decisions, and power outputs over time to minimize operational and startup costs while meeting demand and operational constraints.
example: Decide which generators operate in each time period and how much power they produce to satisfy hourly demand.

problem: Maximum Weight Subset Selection with Pairwise Interactions
description: Select a fixed-size or constrained subset of items to maximize pairwise interaction values counted only when both items in a pair are selected.
example: Choose a subset of items that yields the highest total interaction score among selected pairs.

description: Schedule landing times and landing order for aircraft while satisfying time windows, separation requirements, and early or late landing penalties.
example: Assign landing times to aircraft while observing required separation times and minimizing total deviation penalties.
